core_obligations: Multiply the given relation by the (n-1)-st power of the leading coefficient a_n and rewrite each term so that the powers of t are collected against powers of a_n (proof lines 30706-30712).
Recognise the resulting equation as a monic polynomial relation for the element a_n t with coefficients in R, which is precisely integrality of that element (proof lines 30708-30712).
proof_roadmap: Rescale the given algebraic relation by a power of the leading coefficient (proof lines 30706-30708).
Read off a monic relation for the leading coefficient times t (proof lines 30708-30713).
difficulty_reason: Given a ring map from R to S and an element t of S satisfying a polynomial relation with R-coefficients a_0, ..., a_n the lemma produces an integral element, namely a_n t (statement lines 30697-30703). The proof does not invoke determinants, Cayley-Hamilton or the module of symmetric powers: it multiplies the relation by the (n-1)-st power of the leading coefficient and redistributes the powers of a_n among the terms so that the equation becomes monic in a_n t (proof lines 30705-30713). The exact bookkeeping of that rescaling, especially that the top term becomes the n-th power of a_n t, is the content, and the author writes the whole computation out. H2.
